discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution based on the quantum properties of single photons and entanglement

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the no-cloning property and measurement disturbance of single quanta allow two parties to establish a secret key whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. Ekert (1991) independently showed that entanglement itself can be the resource: a violation of Bell's inequality certifies that no eavesdropper holds the key. That insight linked foundational tests of quantum mechanics directly to a practical technology and anticipated device-independent security. Together these ideas founded quantum communication as a field. They led to experimental key distribution over fibre, free-space links of more than 100 km, and intercontinental distribution by satellite. Above all, this work turned the most puzzling features of quantum physics into a resource and established quantum information as a new branch of physics. It also opened the way to quantum teleportation networks and the future quantum internet.
